+# ADR-007: Portable, self-hosted ATLAS with user-configured agents
+
+- Status: Proposed
+- Date: 2026-10-22
+- Decisions: D13 (platforms), D14 (local and open-weight models), D15 (API-key billing)
+
+## Context
+The Phase 0 design matched one machine:
+- agent roles were fixed to `claude | codex | antigravity` (agent-compatibility.md §5);
+- the platform was macOS only: Keychain, Colima on an APFS volume, Seatbelt and `launchd`;
+- examples used the author's GitHub account.
+
+Other people should be able to run ATLAS with the agents and models *they* have. That includes open-weight models served on their own machine.
+
+## Decision
+
+### 1. Distribution model
+- ATLAS is **self-hosted and single-operator**. Each person installs their own copy and runs it on their own machine with their own accounts.
+- A hosted or multi-user ATLAS that runs work through one person's subscriptions is still a **non-goal**. The provider terms cited in ADR-004 forbid it.
+- No account names, repository names or paths are hard-coded. Docs use placeholders such as `<owner>/<repo>`.
+
+### 2. Agent registry
+Agents are configured by the user, not hard-coded. `~/.atlas/agents.yaml` is global, non-secret, schema-validated and rejects unknown keys:
+
+```yaml
+agents:
+  claude:                         # registry id, referenced by project roles
+    adapter: claude_cli           # a vetted adapter manifest (§3); provider derived: anthropic
+    models: [claude-opus-5-5]     # pinned explicitly (D10); no fallback models
+    billing: subscription         # subscription | api_key | local   (D15)
+  codex:
+    adapter: codex_cli
+    models: [<model id>]
+    billing: subscription
+  antigravity:
+    adapter: manual_handoff
+    declared_family_required: true    # the user's imported result must name its model
+  local-coder:
+    adapter: codex_cli                # same vetted adapter, pointed at a local OSS provider
+    models: [qwen3-coder]
+    model_family: alibaba             # required for any model not in the built-in family map
+    billing: local
+    endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
+  local-reviewer:
+    adapter: openai_compatible_http   # read-only roles only (§4)
+    models: [llama-4-maverick]
+    model_family: meta
+    billing: local
+    endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
+```
+
+Project roles refer to registry ids:
+
+```yaml
+agents: { architect: claude, challenger: codex, developer: codex, reviewer: claude, qa: antigravity }
+```
+
+- **The roles above are a recommended profile, not built-in rules.** The policy engine checks every assignment against the adapter's allowed roles and against ADR-005 independence.
+- A project whose roles can't be satisfied is shown as `BLOCKED(agent_config)`, with the reason.
+- Each agent has three separate identities, all recorded with every artifact: `agent_id` (the registry name), `provider` (who runs inference) and `model_family` (the model's lineage, ADR-005). The provider is derived, never typed by the user:
+  - from the manifest and billing for hosted agents: `anthropic`, `openai`, `google`;
+  - `local` for `billing: local`;

     2	
     3	- Status: Proposed
     4	- Date: 2026-10-22
     5	- Decisions: D13 (platforms), D14 (local and open-weight models), D15 (API-key billing)
     6	
     7	## Context
     8	The Phase 0 design matched one machine:
     9	- agent roles were fixed to `claude | codex | antigravity` (agent-compatibility.md §5);
    10	- the platform was macOS only: Keychain, Colima on an APFS volume, Seatbelt and `launchd`;
    11	- examples used the author's GitHub account.
    12	
    13	Other people should be able to run ATLAS with the agents and models *they* have. That includes open-weight models served on their own machine.
    14	
    15	## Decision
    16	
    17	### 1. Distribution model
    18	- ATLAS is **self-hosted and single-operator**. Each person installs their own copy and runs it on their own machine with their own accounts.
    19	- A hosted or multi-user ATLAS that runs work through one person's subscriptions is still a **non-goal**. The provider terms cited in ADR-004 forbid it.
    20	- No account names, repository names or paths are hard-coded. Docs use placeholders such as `<owner>/<repo>`.
    21	
    22	### 2. Agent registry
    23	Agents are configured by the user, not hard-coded. `~/.atlas/agents.yaml` is global, non-secret, schema-validated and rejects unknown keys:
    24	
    25	```yaml
    26	agents:
    27	  claude:                         # registry id, referenced by project roles
    28	    adapter: claude_cli           # a vetted adapter manifest (§3); provider derived: anthropic
    29	    models: [claude-opus-5-5]     # pinned explicitly (D10); no fallback models
    30	    billing: subscription         # subscription | api_key | local   (D15)
    31	  codex:
    32	    adapter: codex_cli
    33	    models: [<model id>]
    34	    billing: subscription
    35	  antigravity:
    36	    adapter: manual_handoff
    37	    declared_family_required: true    # the user's imported result must name its model
    38	  local-coder:
    39	    adapter: codex_cli                # same vetted adapter, pointed at a local OSS provider
    40	    models: [qwen3-coder]
    41	    model_family: alibaba             # required for any model not in the built-in family map
    42	    billing: local
    43	    endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
    44	  local-reviewer:
    45	    adapter: openai_compatible_http   # read-only roles only (§4)
    46	    models: [llama-4-maverick]
    47	    model_family: meta
    48	    billing: local
    49	    endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
    50	```
    51	
    52	Project roles refer to registry ids:
    53	
    54	```yaml
    55	agents: { architect: claude, challenger: codex, developer: codex, reviewer: claude, qa: antigravity }
    56	```
    57	
    58	- **The roles above are a recommended profile, not built-in rules.** The policy engine checks every assignment against the adapter's allowed roles and against ADR-005 independence.
    59	- A project whose roles can't be satisfied is shown as `BLOCKED(agent_config)`, with the reason.

    62	  - `local` for `billing: local`;

    66	### 3. Adapter manifests (declarative, vetted)

    97	- `billing: subscription` keeps ADR-004 unchanged. The CLI owns its login, and ATLAS strips every provider API-key variable.

   207	### 6.1 Adapter manifest (for `cli` agents)
   208	A manifest is data that the generic `cli` adapter reads. It cannot add code. Fields:

   211	|---|---|

     1	# ADR-005: Review independence is enforced by provider *and* model family
     2	
     3	- Status: Proposed
     4	- Date: 2026-10-22
     5	
     6	## Context
     7	Antigravity can run Claude and GPT-OSS models (`evidence/agy-models.txt`). Claude Code and Codex may also expose models from several families over time. If the reviewer and the author share a model family, they tend to share the same blind spots.
     8	
     9	## Decision
    10	- Every artifact (plan, phase diff, fix) records `author_agent` and `author_model`.
    11	- A reviewer, challenger or QA agent is assigned only if `provider ≠ author provider` **and** `model_family(reviewer_model) ≠ model_family(author_model)`.
    12	- Model family mapping (built-in, versioned with ATLAS):
    13	  - `claude-*` → anthropic;
    14	  - `gpt-*` (including open-weight `gpt-oss-*`), `o*` and Codex defaults → openai;
    15	  - `gemini-*` and `gemma-*` → google;
    16	  - `llama-*` → meta;
    17	  - `qwen*` → alibaba;
    18	  - `mistral-*`, `mixtral-*`, `codestral-*`, `devstral-*` → mistral;
    19	  - `deepseek-*` → deepseek;
    20	  - unknown → `unknown`, which counts as matching the author's family, so independence is not satisfied.
    21	- **Declared family (ADR-007).** A registry entry may set `model_family` for a model the built-in map doesn't know, such as a fine-tune or a renamed local model. The user's declaration is recorded with each artifact. If it contradicts the built-in map, the built-in map wins. A fine-tune counts as the family of its base model.
    22	- **Provider identity (ADR-007 §2).** The "provider ≠ author provider" check compares the *derived* inference provider, not the registry id: `anthropic`, `openai`, `google`, `local`, or the host of an opted-in remote endpoint. Two registry aliases for the same hosted provider never satisfy it.
    23	- **Local exception, stated explicitly.** The provider rule exists so that a single vendor's systems and policies can't both write and judge a change. Models running locally on the operator's own server share no vendor. So when **both** agents have provider `local`, the provider check counts as satisfied, and independence rests on the model-family check alone. In every other case, both checks apply.
    24	- If independence cannot be met, the step goes to `AWAITING_MANUAL` or `BLOCKED`. The author is never used as the sole reviewer.
    25	- A fix to a finding is "verified" only by an independent reviewer's re-check on the new SHA, plus re-executed tests.
    26	
    27	## Consequences
    28	- With user-configured agents, any profile is accepted only if every review, challenge and QA assignment passes these rules. A profile with a single model family can't run mandatory reviews, so those steps go to `AWAITING_MANUAL`.
    29	- With the default roles, the developer is Codex (openai), the code reviewer is Claude (anthropic), and QA is Antigravity on a Gemini model (google). That gives three distinct families.
    30	- Losing one provider may block mandatory reviews. This is intentional, because the brief requires that independence never be sacrificed.
     1	# ADR-004: Agents are invoked only as unmodified official CLIs via subprocess
     2	
     3	> Amended by [ADR-007](ADR-007-portable-pluggable-providers.md): ATLAS is self-hosted and single-operator, agents come from a user-configured registry, and API-key billing is an explicit per-agent opt-in (D15).
     4	
     5	- Status: Proposed
     6	- Date: 2026-10-22
     7	
     8	## Decision
     9	- Agent CLIs (built-in: Claude Code and Codex) are run as their unmodified binaries (`claude -p …`, `codex exec …`), as the logged-in OS user, with subscription login managed solely by those CLIs. Other CLIs plug in only through vetted adapter manifests (ADR-007 §3).
    10	- ATLAS never reads, copies, stores or proxies the subscription credentials that CLIs manage. The only provider credentials it stores are API keys the user explicitly gives it for an agent configured with `billing: api_key` (ADR-007 §5). It never uses the Agent SDK with subscription credentials, never runs browser automation and never calls provider HTTP endpoints directly.
    11	- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CODEX_API_KEY` and other provider key variables are stripped from every agent environment, so billing cannot silently switch to an API account. The one exception is an agent configured with `billing: api_key`: only that agent's own process receives its own key, under the variable its manifest names.
    12	- ATLAS is self-hosted and single-operator: anyone may run their own copy with their own accounts. It must not be offered as a hosted or multi-user service that uses anyone else's subscription. [Claude terms](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance) (excerpts saved in [`evidence/claude-legal-compliance-2026-10-22.md`](../evidence/claude-legal-compliance-2026-10-22.md)) forbid third-party developers routing requests through Free/Pro/Max credentials "on behalf of their users". They explicitly allow "an end user … signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own Claude subscription". Self-hosted ATLAS is that case: each operator runs their own copy with their own login, and ATLAS never collects, stores or intermediates Claude.ai credentials. A hosted ATLAS would also fall under the Commercial Terms conditions (unmodified binary, no intermediated billing). That is a further reason the non-goal stands. The page also says Pro/Max usage limits "assume ordinary, individual usage"; ATLAS's single-operator, one-invocation-per-agent default is designed with that in mind.
    13	- Codex (any agent using the `codex_cli` manifest, whatever its billing; D5 unchanged by ADR-007) on **public** repositories is blocked, with no override in this release (D5). [OpenAI docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) say: "Do not use this workflow for public or open-source repositories."
    14	
    15	## Consequences
    16	- Startup capability probes and version pinning cover CLI flag drift.
    17	- Exact quota numbers are unavailable. The capacity state is inferred from documented signals only.
